To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a new UV strobe light epifluorescence optical system with a dye that stains DNA permits the evaluation of sperm motion characteristics of fresh and frozen semen in a simple medium, in a milk-based cryoprotectant, and even in milk.
the use of Hoechst stain with UV epifluorescence and strobe light illumination allows the evaluation of sperm motility and morphology in whole milk extenders and other complex semen extenders.

the use of Hoechst staining with UV light permits evaluation of bull sperm frozen in a whole milk extender and that the motion characteristics are similar to those of sperm in an egg yolk-glycerol-Tris extender.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a new epifluoresent optics system with a strobe lamp for the analysis of living sperm stained with Hoechs 33342 dye.
the development of procedures for evaluating living sperm stained with Hoechs 33342 while they are in a simple medium or commonly used extenders that contain static nonsperm particulate material.
the evaluation of living sperm stained with the fluorescent dye Hoechst 33258.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new epiflurescent system with the UV light source is capable of evaluating stained sperm in the presence of nonsperm particulate material.
the use of the new epiflurescent optics with Hoechst dye is a useful tool for evaluating sperm motion characteristics in a simple medium, in egg yolk-based extenders and in whole milk.

the use of the new UV epifluorescence optical system with a strobe illumination source permits the use of DNA staining of bull spermatozoa in milk and other complex extenders and provides an alternative to the use of the expensive and cumbersome laser-based systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new epiflourescent optics, with UV light, and the dye, Hoechst 33,342, are effective for measuring sperm motion characteristics of living sperm in the presence of static particles.
staining of sperm with 2.5 to 10 microg/ml of the dye in simple medium, or with 40 to 50 microg/ml in complex extenders, is an effective means of evaluating live sperm.
the new epiflorescent system with UV illumination is a useful tool for analyzing stained sperm in complex media.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to evaluate sperm motion characteristics in the presence of static particles.

the dye concentrations, exposure times, and epifluorescence optics developed for use with this stain facilitate evaluation of bull sperm frozen in whole milk, which should be useful for evaluating sperm from other species when nonsperm particles may interfere.
the use of a UV epifluorescence light source and a strobe light to illuminate the sample is critical to the success of this approach.
